video_metadata.working_title: MASSACHUSETTS 1969 Cold Case — DNA Identified Her Killer After 49 Years | Jane Britton
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: In January 1969 Harvard anthropology graduate student Jane Sanders Britton, 23, was raped and killed in her Cambridge apartment; a red-ochre detail fed a campus rumor about a professor for decades, until in November 2018 the Middlesex District Attorney announced that DNA had identified Michael Sumpter, a career criminal who died in 2001 and was never charged in her death.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: grief, unease at how rumor replaced fact for 49 years, then sober relief

protagonist._instructions: The main character of your story - can be hero, villain, or antihero. Fill with verified facts only.
protagonist.full_name: Jane Sanders Britton (victim, heart of the story)
protagonist.occupation_or_status: Graduate student in anthropology at Harvard University; Radcliffe College alumna (class of 1967)
protagonist.location: Fourth-floor apartment, 6 University Road, Cambridge, Massachusetts, near Harvard Square
protagonist.physical_description: Not used in the script beyond real archival photos.
protagonist.background_brief: Born in 1945 in Boston and raised in Needham, Massachusetts. Her father, J. Boyd Britton, was administrative vice president of Radcliffe College (Harvard Crimson 1969 article quoted on Websleuths; secondary). She had a brother, Boyd (described in 2018 as her surviving brother). She was part of the Harvard Peabody Museum team excavating Tepe Yahya in southeastern Iran in 1968. She was due to sit her general examinations in anthropology on January 7, 1969, the day she was found.
protagonist.psychological_profile: Described by reviewers of Becky Cooper's book as independent, strong, outspoken and outgoing; Cooper wrote that she was hard to pin down in a simple description (paraphrase, Harvard Crimson review).
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: On her last evening she had dinner with anthropology classmates and went ice skating on the Common with her boyfriend; after midnight she stopped in at her neighbors' for a glass of sherry.

chronological_timeline._instructions: List every significant event with exact dates when possible. This is the backbone of your script.

events.what_happened: Jane Sanders Britton born; grows up in Needham
Michael Eugene Sumpter born
Jane graduates (Radcliffe class of 1967) and continues as a Harvard anthropology graduate student
Sumpter works on Arrow Street, about a mile from Jane's later apartment
Jane is among the excavators on the Harvard Peabody Museum dig directed by Karl Lamberg-Karlovsky
Jane and Humphries have dinner with anthropology classmates, then go ice skating on the Common; they return to her apartment around 10:30 p.m.; he leaves around 11:30 p.m.
Jane visits neighbors the Mitchells for sherry; time-of-death window later put at roughly 12:30 to 1:30 a.m. per Wikipedia infobox (window not officially confirmed)
Anthropology general exams held; Humphries takes his; Jane does not appear
Humphries knocks; no answer; with neighbor Donald Mitchell he enters the unlocked apartment and finds Jane dead, face down on her bed, partly covered by blankets and a fur coat

Autopsy: sexual assault and multiple blows to the head with a blunt object; weapon never identified. Red ochre powder found on her body and in the apartment; press speculation about a 'primitive rite' rejected by police and Harvard anthropologists. Swabs taken at autopsy are preserved.
Investigation focuses on people around her (students, faculty); no charges; a campus rumor about a professor grows for decades
Sumpter arrested and later convicted of assaulting a woman he met at the Harvard Square MBTA station
Ellen Rutchick, 23, raped and killed (DA release says January 6; Wikipedia January 5)
Mary Lee McClain, 24, sexually assaulted and killed
Sumpter commits a rape for which he receives a 15-to-20-year sentence
events.significance: Why his DNA ended up in CODIS

events.location: Boston (Lemuel Shattuck Hospital correctional unit per Wikipedia; other reports say paroled into hospice)
events.what_happened: Sumpter dies of cancer, age 54
events.significance: Never tried for any of the murders

events.what_happened: Rutchick family asks Boston Police Cold Case Squad to review her case
Profile from old slides in Rutchick case hits Sumpter's CODIS profile; Suffolk DA told in 2010 and announces him as prime suspect
Suffolk DA Daniel Conley and Commissioner Edward Davis announce Sumpter as the assailant in the McClain case
Becky Cooper first hears the rumor as an undergraduate (2009); returns in 2012 and audits Lamberg-Karlovsky's class
events.significance: The writer who would not let go

events.what_happened: Boston Globe reports Middlesex DA refuses to release files citing an active investigation; state supervisor of records repeatedly orders release or better explanation; Cooper and Michael Widmer keep pressing
Lab obtains, for the first time, a Y-STR (male-specific) profile from the remaining DNA on the original autopsy swabs
Lab notifies investigators of a match between the Y-STR profile and Sumpter's CODIS sample
Investigators locate Sumpter's brother through Ancestry.com; the brother cooperates and gives a fresh DNA sample that further confirms the match; the brother is excluded as contributor
DA Marian Ryan announces DNA identified Sumpter; describes window entry; calls it the oldest case her office has solved; case closed
Becky Cooper publishes We Keep the Dead Close; reviewers note the rumor proves false

events.what_happened: No reported developments; case remains closed by the Middlesex DA; Sumpter was never charged or convicted

cold_open_material._instructions: The most dramatic moment of your story - this will be your hook.

the_moment.what_is_happening: Jane's boyfriend knocks at her fourth-floor door after she misses the general exams; no answer; he and a neighbor go in
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: A 23-year-old Harvard scholar killed in her bed a few blocks from Harvard Square; red ochre powder on her body
the_moment.ironic_twist: For 49 years the story people told was about a professor and an ancient ritual; the DNA pointed to a stranger who had worked about a mile away

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: Who killed Jane Britton, and why did a rumor outlive the truth for almost half a century?

the_method._instructions: How did the protagonist do what they did? Technical details that can be explained to a general audience.
the_method.technique_name: Y-STR DNA profiling plus CODIS search, confirmed with a relative located through Ancestry.com
step_by_step_explanation: Swabs collected at the 1969 autopsy were preserved.
In October 2017 the Massachusetts State Police Crime Lab developed a Y-STR profile, which reads markers only on the male Y chromosome, from the remaining DNA.
The profile was compared with offender profiles in CODIS; in July 2018 it matched Sumpter's stored sample (described as a 'soft hit').

Because a Y-STR profile is shared by men in the same paternal line, investigators found Sumpter's brother via Ancestry.com; his fresh sample further confirmed the match and he was excluded as the contributor.
The DA announced the identification and closed the case.
the_method.why_it_worked: Sumpter's profile was already in CODIS from his rape conviction; the new Y-STR test could read a male profile in a tiny, old, mixed sample.

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: A DNA test that reads only the Y chromosome, passed father to son almost unchanged, like a family surname.
The FBI-run national index of DNA profiles from convicted offenders and crime scenes.
A lead-level match that must be confirmed before being called an identification.

the_method.scale_of_operation: One set of 49-year-old swabs; per Cooper, the testing used up the remaining crime-scene DNA

systemic_failure._instructions: What institution, system, or authority failed to prevent this?
systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: Investigation and record keeping across agencies; campus culture of rumor
systemic_failure.how_they_were_supposed_to_protect: Investigate, inform the family and public
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: 1969 science could not read the evidence; focus on the anthropology circle; rumor filled the silence; files withheld for decades
specific_incompetence_examples: Sumpter's DNA linked to a 1972 Boston murder in 2009 and a 1973 murder in 2012, but the Britton swabs produced no usable profile until October 2017
State supervisor of records repeatedly ordered the DA's office to release portions or explain the withholding (2017)
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The 'ritual' red ochre fed half a century of gossip; reporting later suggested it may have come from Jane's own art supplies (secondary source, uncertain)

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Cambridge Police (1969), Massachusetts State Police assigned to the Middlesex DA; MSP Crime Lab
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: That the killer came from Jane's academic circle; ritual theory
the_investigation.key_breakthrough: October 2017 Y-STR profile; July 2018 CODIS match
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: Sumpter's later 1975 rape conviction put his DNA in the offender database
the_investigation.how_long_until_caught: Never caught; identified 49 years after the crime, 17 years after his death

the_confrontation._instructions: The arrest, raid, or climactic moment when everything collapses.
the_confrontation.scene_description: DA Ryan announces the identification and closes the case; Boyd Britton issues a statement
the_confrontation.protagonist_reaction: Sumpter had died in 2001; no reaction possible
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: No arrest, no trial, no defense; an identification, not a conviction

charges_filed: None in the Britton case; Sumpter died in 2001

victim_impact_statements.key_quote: Paraphrase: the DNA match may be all the family ever gets as a conclusion; learning to understand and forgive remains a challenge

legal_resolution.current_status: Case closed by the Middlesex DA (Nov 20, 2018). Sumpter was identified by DNA according to the DA but was never charged, tried or convicted; he is legally presumed innocent. No developments found as of October 2026.
